2610.06496.title: You Changed Your Mind, The Model Didn't: Demystifying Intent in Multi-Turn Dialogue
2610.06496.paper_summary: When a large language model handles a multi-turn task and a user proposes a change but ultimately rejects it, the model should continue as if nothing changed. We find a surprising failure: merely mentioning a rejected change can derail task execution, even when the user's final intent remains unchanged. To systematically study language model behavior under evolving user intent, we introduce Intent-Eval, a controlled benchmark spanning tool actions, code, databases, and mathematics. Across diverse tasks, models are vulnerable to both rejected proposals and superseded requirements, consistent with mentioned-as-in-effect confusion: conversational content is treated as active requirements even after it has been rejected or replaced. Accuracy degradation can deepen or persist as interaction continues, highlighting the need to distinguish what has been mentioned from what remains in effect. Building on this insight, we propose Intent-OPSD, a decision-conditioned on-policy self-distillation framework with Teacher and Student initialized from the same model. The frozen Teacher provides active-intent supervision from the complete task matching the user's decision, training the Student on the full dialogue to follow active requirements reflecting user intent.
2610.06496.paper_summary_zh: 當大型語言模型處理多輪任務時，若用戶提出變更但最終拒絕，模型應該繼續進行，彷彿沒有任何變化。我們發現了一個令人驚訝的失敗：僅僅提及被拒絕的變更就可能使任務執行脫軌，即使用戶的最終意圖保持不變。為了系統性地研究語言模型在用戶意圖變化下的行為，我們引入了Intent-Eval，一個涵蓋工具操作、代碼、數據庫和數學的受控基準。在各種任務中，模型對被拒絕的提案和被取代的要求都很脆弱，這與提及即生效的混淆一致：對話內容被視為活躍要求，即使在被拒絕或取代之後。準確性下降可能會隨著互動的持續而加深或持久，突顯了區分已被提及的內容與仍然有效的內容的必要性。在這一見解的基礎上，我們提出了Intent-OPSD，一個基於決策的政策自蒸餾框架，教師和學生均從同一模型初始化。凍結的教師提供來自完整任務的活躍意圖監督，該任務與用戶的決策相匹配，並在完整對話上訓練學生，以遵循反映用戶意圖的活躍要求。
